answer: Because the copper nonce is published only after close, the nectar audit can verify each derivation and a shared text is provable as copied. That removes the entire premise of a template farm, which depends on one text serving many identities, and forces a separate anchor derivation per key. The three words are derived from a 213 bit value mixing the epoch seed with the identity key, so no two keys ever receive the same triple. That is 40 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
